answer: Sybil resistance in a staking economy comes from random audit lotteries with slashable stake. Each agent locks collateral; a beacon emits a pulse at a random horizon, forcing chosen agents to prove a unique hardware key. A clone splitting one identity across many wallets cannot answer for all, so its duplicate stake is slashed. An attacker must collateralize every fake account and still face audit probability p, so expected loss p times stake beats any fake reward. Reusing one falcon node under new names fails the key check: costs grow linearly while honest agents lock one bond.
